articles.title: Another earthquake in Panama after 7.6 magnitude quake that collapsed buildings, sent crowds running for safety
articles.summary: A fresh 6.0-magnitude earthquake struck 7 km north of La Tronosa in Panama, the US Geological Survey (USGS) reported, following a powerful quake that
articles.body: A fresh 6.0-magnitude earthquake struck 7 km north of La Tronosa in Panama, the US Geological Survey (USGS) reported, following a powerful quake that shook the country's southern coast on Friday. The earlier tremor sent people rushing out of shopping malls and buildings as the ground shook, while videos circulating on social media showed a television broadcast being interrupted and residents fleeing to safety.The US Geological Survey (USGS) initially estimated the earthquake's magnitude at 8.0 before revising it to 7.6. Other reports put the magnitude at 7.7. The quake struck at a depth of around 10 kilometres, with its epicentre about 200 kilometres southwest of Panama City.Footage shared on social media showed people evacuating buildings and gathering outdoors amid fears of further tremors. In Penonomé, a city between the epicentre and the capital, videos showed vehicles and trees swaying during the earthquake.The tremors prompted precautionary evacuations, while schools were closed and two metro lines in Panama City were suspended for safety checks. The earthquake was also felt in neighbouring Costa Rica, according to Reuters.Despite the intensity of the shaking, Panama appeared to have avoided widespread destruction in the immediate aftermath. President Raul Mulino said no deaths had been documented as of Friday evening, although he cautioned that the situation could change as assessments continued.Buildings damaged, residents flee outdoorsThe earthquake caused damage in several provinces, including Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos, according to Panama's civil protection service, as reported by The Associated Press.Omar Smith of the civil protection service said several people had been injured, including one person struck by debris in Penonomé. Cracks were also reported along roads in Veraguas.In Penonomé, the bell tower of a cathedral collapsed, while other buildings were damaged. President Mulino travelled to the city to assess the situation.In Panama City, residents rushed into streets, parks and open spaces as a precaution. Offices and commercial buildings were evacuated, with people remaining outdoors amid concerns about aftershocks.Rosendo Domínguez, 60, who is from Herrera province, told AP by phone that objects had fallen over in his kitchen.“Everyone is outside, scared,” he said.A resident of the San Francisco district of Panama City also described the shaking as strong enough to make buildings sway and send water spilling out of swimming pools.Tsunami alerts issued, then liftedThe earthquake prompted tsunami alerts across parts of Central and South America. The US Tsunami Warning System initially identified a potential threat to coastal areas of Panama, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Peru, Mexico, Guatemala, Nicaragua, Colombia and Ecuador.The US Embassy in Panama warned that aftershocks capable of causing damage could follow the earthquake and cautioned people near the coast about possible surges and strong currents.“Strong and unusual currents and unpredictable surges may occur along the shore,” the embassy said, advising people in affected areas to stay away from damaged structures and follow official guidance.The tsunami warning for the coasts of Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala was subsequently lifted, AP reported. Alerts for El Salvador and Chile's Easter Island were also lifted.Nestor Luque of the University of Panama said waves of one to three metres were expected near Isla Canas and the southern coast of Los Santos. Seawater was also reported to have reached homes on Isla Canas.Airport reopens, Panama Canal operationalTocumen International Airport resumed operations on Friday afternoon after a temporary suspension. The Panama Canal Authority said canal operations continued as normal while teams inspected facilities for potential damage.More than 40 aftershocks were reported following the main earthquake, Reuters said. AP reported that some measured magnitudes of 5.8, 5.5 and 5.2.The USGS estimated that around 43,000 people in Panama lived in areas exposed to severe or greater shaking. It also projected potential economic losses ranging from 1% to 10% of the country's gross domestic product.Electricity provider Naturgy reported power outages across six provinces.Panama was scheduled to conduct a nationwide evacuation drill the following Monday to test emergency preparedness.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Rahul's INDI Alliance and Kejriwal's CJP': BJP accuses protesters of plotting to destabilise India ahead of Jantar Mantar protest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday accused the INDIA bloc led by Rahul Gandhi and associates of Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday accused the INDIA bloc led by Rahul Gandhi and associates of Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal of attempting to destabilise the country, alleging that they were pursuing their political agendas at the behest of foreign forces.Addressing a press conference in Delhi, Nabin described the situation as “highly dangerous and serious” and alleged that two groups were competing to create instability in the country.“Who is doing this? Two anarchic groups: one led by Rahul Gandhi of the ‘INDI Alliance’, and the other led by Arvind Kejriwal’s associates, CJP,” he said.Nabin claimed that the groups had been rejected by the public and accused them of attempting to undermine national stability instead of accepting the people's verdict.“These are people that the public has rejected... instead of accepting that verdict or learning from it, you have hatched a plot to destabilize the country,” he said.The BJP president further alleged that the groups were acting at the behest of foreign forces. However, he did not identify the alleged foreign actors or provide evidence supporting the charge in the statement provided.Nabin also linked his allegations to India's development trajectory, saying the country was continuing to progress despite persistent global crises.“You cannot digest India's growth, progress, and advancement. You cannot bear to see India moving forward as a self-reliant and empowered nation,” he said, adding that Indian democracy was strong enough to thwart attempts to destabilise the country.Separately, Bihar minister Ram Kripal Yadav accused CJP of attempting to mislead students and create unrest for political gains. He described the organisation as unregistered and questioned its political credentials.“CJP is an unregistered organisation. It is merely a group of such people who, under the leadership of a few politicians, are trying to misguide children just to establish themselves,” Yadav said in Patna.He alleged that the group was being used by opposition parties to advance their political interests.“They are doing this solely to glorify their leadership and establish their party which, being unregistered, cannot even be called a political party, as it lacks recognition,” he said.Yadav further alleged that the opposition was using CJP as a front to target the government, adding that its members were not acting in the national interest.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: New Zealand squad for India series 2026: Full team lists for NZ vs IND T20I series
articles.summary: New Zealand have named a 16-member squad for the 5-match T20I series vs India. Mitchell Santner captains, Rachin Ravindra misses out, and Adam Milne returns.
articles.body:
New Zealand have named a 16-member T20I squad for the five-match home series against India beginning October 22 in Christchurch.

Rachin Ravindra has been ruled out with a dislocated shoulder, targeting a return for the ODI series beginning November 4 in Auckland.

Finn Allen and Tim Seifert reunite as openers, with Adam Milne and Michael Bracewell returning after missing the T20 World Cup through injury.

New Zealand T20I squad vs India: Rachin Ravindra out, Adam Milne and Michael Bracewell return under Mitchell Santner

New Zealand's home summer kicks off with one of the most anticipated white-ball series of the year, and they've announced a 16-member group for the five-match T20I series against India.

White-ball captain Mitchell Santner will lead the squad across five T20Is beginning October 22 at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. The series spans four cities over 11 days and is the opening leg of India's comprehensive 12-match tour of New Zealand, which also includes five ODIs and two Tests.

New Zealand Cricket confirmed that more than 76,000 tickets had already been sold for the tour with a full month still to go before the first ball is bowled.

Thirteen T20 World Cup players retained; two return from injury

The selection shows a thread of continuity from New Zealand's T20 World Cup campaign earlier this year, where they reached the final before falling to India. Thirteen members of that squad have been retained, with two significant additions in the form of spin all-rounder Michael Bracewell and experienced pacer Adam Milne, both of whom missed the tournament through injury.

Milne slots into an already well-stocked pace attack alongside Lockie Ferguson, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson and Jacob Duffy. Young pacers Zak Foulkes and Nathan Smith round out a seven-strong seam unit that gives New Zealand variety and depth in the format.

Ravindra ruled out of T20Is, targeting ODI return

The most significant absence from the squad is Rachin Ravindra, who has been ruled out after dislocating his right shoulder during a promotional shoot last week.

The injury is expected to keep him sidelined for around six weeks, with the target being a return to action for the ODI series beginning November 4 at Eden Park in Auckland.

Ben Sears, meanwhile, was not considered due to ongoing ankle rehabilitation. Pace star Will O'Rourke also misses out with an injury to his left hamstring and calf.

Allen and Seifert reunite to form explosive opening partnership

Finn Allen and Tim Seifert will come out again at the top of the order. The pair haven't batted together for New Zealand since their joint campaign at this year's T20 World Cup, and what they produced there remains fresh in the memory.

Allen blasted an unbeaten 33-ball century against South Africa in the semi-final at Eden Gardens as New Zealand cruised to a nine-wicket win.

Seifert contributed 58 off 33 balls in that same match and had arguably the best tournament of his international career, later winning the Player of the Tournament award in The Hundred after scoring 394 runs at a 168 strike rate, including a match-winning 72 off 38 balls in the final.

articles.title: California sends 'illegal' notice to company with 'Terminator'-like robot; CEO posts the letter online, celebrates: 'We made...'
articles.summary: California's combat sports regulator has told a San Francisco start-up to stop putting humans in a cage with its robots.
articles.body: California's combat sports regulator has told a San Francisco start-up to stop putting humans in a cage with its robots. The order comes weeks after one of the company's steel humanoids, built to look like the original Terminator, sent a YouTuber flying across its octagon in front of a cheering crowd.The California State Athletic Commission sent the cease-and-desist letter on September 30 to REK, short for Robot Entertainment Kombat, over its unsanctioned "Human vs Robot" event on September 18. Chief executive Cix Liv did not sound worried. He posted the letter on X the same day with a short caption: "We made it, boys."The letter says any boxing or mixed martial arts contest, match or exhibition involving a human in California needs the commission's approval first. Promoting or taking part in one without a licence, it adds, is a misdemeanour under section 18640 of the state's Business and Professions Code.Liv has a counterargument ready. He says the law defines a match as one between two persons, and a humanoid is not a person. The state, he says, is welcome to argue otherwise in court.Frankie LaPenna won two of his three human vs robot fightsThe human in question was Frankie LaPenna, a YouTuber with over 9 million followers who is known for videos of himself getting hurt. He fought three robots that night. The first, a smaller Unitree G1, went down within seconds.Then came two modified EngineAI T800s, which REK says stand about 6 feet tall, kick with up to 850 pounds of force and wear a mechanical skull with glowing red eyes. One of them landed a blow that left LaPenna sprawled on the far side of the cage, motorcycle-style protective gear and all. He got back up and shoved the robot to the floor to win.His last opponent, a quicker robot REK calls "Predator", beat him by getting up every time he dropped it. LaPenna left with an injured hand from punching a metal frame, after signing a waiver that cleared REK if he died.Every robot in the cage had a human pilot at the controlsNone of the robots were fighting on their own. Pilots steered them in real time using VR headsets or a gamepad, much like flying a drone, while AI from REK's technology partner Reflex Arc kept them balanced and handled trained movements. So every strike aimed at LaPenna was a person's decision.California's combat sports rules were never written for robot opponentsNeither California nor federal law explicitly bans human versus robot fights. The commission said unsanctioned events put the physical and financial wellbeing of everyone involved at risk, and that it would consider fresh guidance as robot technology evolves.That could take time. Combat sports are regulated state by state in the US, and lawyers in the field say most commissions would need new rules before they could shut such events down.REK calls itself a humanoid robot fighting league. It has staged 14 events across nine cities, including private shows at the OpenAI and xAI offices, and says more than 20,000 fights have been played on its simulator across 65 countries. Liv says there are no plans to repeat the human fight.Its next show, the sold-out REK Deathmatch in San Francisco on October 9, was billed as the first fight between humanoids carrying blades. articles.title: History buffs create 'Bayeux Tapestry' of village
articles.summary: A Norfolk village showcases significant events since 1066 on a five-metre long cloth.
articles.body:
A village is hoping to interest more people in local history with the creation of its own "Bayeux Tapestry".

Inspired by the 70-metre long artwork which is currently on loan to the British Museum, history buffs in Hockham, Norfolk, commissioned their own printed cloth version which starts with the 1066 Norman Conquest and the mention of their village in the Domesday Book of 1086.

The 5m (16ft)-long cloth details other significant events such as the granting of its market charter and soldiers returning from World War One.

"They really show what life's been like over the past few hundred years," said Chris Garrod, of the Hockham History group.

"Some of the dates are from records from the local record office - when the first Zeppelin [airship] was seen over the village, that sort of thing."

Members of the society sourced local books and photos of events, buildings and people to depict on the tapestry, including the former reading rooms which once stood on the village green before being demolished in the 1960s.

The village church and the Edinburgh village hall are also pictured.

"I think anybody who's seen it for the first time has just been stunned by the quality of it. It's fantastic, really colourful, beautiful," said Garrod.

"We've nicknamed it the Hockham Tapestry, even though it's not a tapestry. It's a bit of poetic licence."

The images were all created by artist Emily Brownlow, using computer design software.

Brownlow, who has lived in the village "on and off" since the age of two is also a "very enthusiastic" member of the local history club.

She said: "I just hope everybody gets to come in and learn something, even the people that are really deep into the history of the place and find a couple of bits on there that they didn't know."

The group took only two weeks to decide on the content and the imagery for the "tapestry" before it went to the printers, who charged them £100 for the work.

The "tapestry" has been installed in Holy Trinity Church and is on display on Saturday and Sunday for the history weekend. What happens to it after that is yet to be decided.

An exhibition about the Bayeux Tapestry (but not featuring the actual woven artwork itself) is touring Britain, and visits Norwich Castle Museum & Art Gallery, 12 November-10 January.
